item.title: Yamanashi Prefectural Museum: The Region's History, Nature and Culture — Guide
item.description: The Yamanashi Prefectural Museum presents the region’s history, natural environment and culture through engaging, hands-on exhibits, themed around the long relationship between the people of Yamanashi and the land they live on, from the mountains and rivers to the wine and craft traditions. Set within a spacious park with outdoor areas to explore, the museum is designed to be accessible and interactive, making it a good indoor option for families and for visitors wanting deeper context on the region beyond its famous Mount Fuji views.

item.title: Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum: One of the World's Top Three Dinosaur Museums — Guide
item.description: The Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum is considered one of the world’s top three dinosaur museums, housed in a striking dome-shaped building and showcasing full dinosaur skeletons, fossils and interactive exhibits, many excavated from Fukui itself, which has proven to be one of Japan’s richest dinosaur fossil sites. The museum displays around 50 full dinosaur skeletons alongside detailed exhibits on prehistoric life, and visitors can also join guided tours to an actual fossil excavation site nearby to see ongoing palaeontological work in progress.

item.title: Fukui Prefectural Natural History Museum: Local Ecology and Natural Science — Guide
item.description: The Fukui Prefectural Natural History Museum offers a broader look at the prefecture’s natural science beyond dinosaurs, covering local ecology, geology and wildlife through hands-on exhibits and displays that give visitors a fuller picture of Fukui’s natural environment across different eras. Considerably smaller and less visited than the famous Dinosaur Museum, it makes a good complementary stop for visitors with a genuine interest in natural history rather than dinosaurs alone, or a manageable outing for families with younger children.

item.title: Gunma Safari Park: A Drive-Through Wildlife Encounter — Guide
item.description: Gunma Safari Park lets visitors experience a drive-through safari within Japan, with lions, tigers, bears and other large animals roaming semi-freely across expansive enclosures that vehicles pass through at a slow, controlled pace. Visitors can drive their own car (following strict safety guidelines) or ride a park safari bus for a more guided experience, while a separate walking zoo section offers closer encounters with smaller animals, feeding experiences, and a petting zone suited to younger children.

item.title: Nasu Animal Kingdom: A Highland Wildlife Park for Families — Guide
item.description: Nasu Animal Kingdom is one of the largest and most popular family attractions in the Nasu Highlands, combining indoor and outdoor zones across a sprawling site that houses a wide range of animals from big cats to farmyard favourites. The park is known for its close-up encounter opportunities, including a petting zone with rabbits and small mammals, along with scheduled dog agility shows and bird-of-prey flight demonstrations that run throughout the day, making it a reliable full-day option for families visiting the highlands.

item.title: Tobu World Square: 100+ World Landmarks in Miniature — Guide
item.description: Tobu World Square is a unique outdoor theme park displaying over 100 miniature reproductions of the world’s most famous landmarks and Japanese UNESCO World Heritage sites, each built at a precise 1/25 scale with astonishing architectural detail, down to tiny figurines populating the scenes. Visitors can walk past miniature versions of the Egyptian pyramids, the Taj Mahal, Tokyo Skytree and Nikko’s own Toshogu shrine in a single afternoon, making it a memorable and easily digestible stop for families and architecture enthusiasts alike.

item.title: Railway Museum, Omiya: A Century of Japanese Trains — Guide
item.description: The Railway Museum in Omiya, operated by JR East, is one of Japan’s largest and most comprehensive train museums, home to dozens of historic locomotives and rolling stock spanning from Meiji-era steam engines to early Shinkansen bullet trains. Interactive exhibits, a large train diorama with model railways, a driving simulator and a panoramic observation deck overlooking the Tohoku Shinkansen line make it a favourite for train enthusiasts and families alike.
